method: Highest-conviction dossiers for the week of 2026-09-07, drawn from the scored book plus new names surfaced by this week's discovery pass. Levels are anchored to the real 52-week range off the Fri 2026-09-04 close; sell > buy > stop on every idea.

ideas.why: The single widest gap in the book between what the business printed and what the tape pays for it. Broadcom just guided AI revenue to $58bn this year, $115bn next and $230bn in FY28, and the shares still sit 27.7% below their 52-week high at 357.90. You are being paid to wait for the multiple to catch up to the disclosure.
bull: FY28 AI revenue framed at $230bn against $58bn this year - if even two-thirds lands, today's 357.90 is a fraction of fair value.
Six XPU customers named including OpenAI and Anthropic; custom accelerators are multi-year programmes, not spot orders.
27.7% below the 495.00 52-week high while earnings compound at +86% - the de-rating is a multiple story, not a business story.
bear: Customer concentration is extreme: a single hyperscaler pushing an XPU programme out a year would gut the FY27 bridge.
The 5-yr Treasury printed a fresh 52-week high at 4.545% on Friday - long-duration growth multiples keep compressing while the curve does that.
Guiding AI revenue three years out invites a miss; the market has already shown it will de-rate first and check later.
ideas.inv: If AI revenue growth decelerates below ~100% y/y or a named XPU customer exits, the FY27/FY28 bridge breaks and the thesis is void.
ideas.thesis: Q3 FY26 on Sep 2 printed $29.6bn revenue, +86% y/y, with operating income up 92% and adjusted EPS $3.32 vs $3.24 consensus. AI semiconductor revenue alone was $16.7bn, +221% y/y, across six XPU customers including Google, OpenAI and Anthropic. Custom-silicon design wins are multi-year and sticky, and the VMware software base funds the buyback.

ideas.why: Four insiders put $9.49m of their own money into this at $48.26 on Aug 25, and it closed Friday at 47.80 - 1.0% below their price. It rose 1.81% on a day healthcare fell 1.04% as a sector. A 56.3% drawdown with a four-person insider cluster underneath it is the clearest risk/reward setup in this book.
bull: Four insiders bought $9.49m at $48.26 on Aug 25 - it closed Friday 1.0% below their price.
Rose 1.81% on Friday while healthcare was the second-worst sector at -1.04%.
56.3% below the 52-week high on a device business whose procedure volumes grow with demographics.
bear: A 56.3% drawdown of that magnitude usually reflects something real - insiders can be early and wrong.
Only 13.3% above the 52-week low; the downtrend has not been broken on the chart.
Healthcare as a sector is out of favour and fell 1.04% on Friday.
ideas.inv: A break below the 42.20 52-week low would mean the insider cluster was wrong about the bottom - exit rather than average down.
ideas.thesis: a medical-device business with a strong electrophysiology franchise and consistent procedure-volume-driven growth. Devices are less exposed to patent cliffs than pharmaceuticals, and the revenue base compounds with an ageing population rather than with the economy.

ideas.why: A $95bn AI-server backlog - a record, and disclosed rather than forecast - alongside 58% revenue growth and 203% EPS growth. The stock broke a three-month consolidation with a 15.81% single-session move to a 52-week high. This is the clearest evidence in the book that AI capex is being spent rather than announced.
bull: Record $95.0bn AI-server backlog is disclosed revenue, not a forecast.
Q2 FY2027 revenue $47.0bn (+58% y/y) and EPS $7.04 (+203% y/y), with FY guidance raised.
Fox Advisors upgrade to Outperform, $625 target - about 19% above Friday's 524.14.
bear: Server assembly margins are thin; converting backlog into profit is not the same as converting it into revenue.
2.0% below the 52-week high after a 15.81% single-session move - the easy money is gone.
AI-server backlog can be cancelled or deferred; it is an order book, not a contract portfolio.
ideas.inv: If AI-server gross margins compress as the backlog converts, revenue growth will not translate into earnings and the re-rate reverses.
ideas.thesis: AI-server assembly is a lower-margin business than semiconductors, which is the honest caveat - but Dell has the enterprise relationships and the supply-chain scale to convert AI demand into volume nobody else can match. The storage and PC businesses fund the working capital that AI servers consume.

ideas.why: Memory stopped being a commodity this quarter. NAND prices up ~55% q/q and DRAM up 385% y/y with Micron's leading-edge capacity already spoken for through December means the next two prints are largely pre-sold at known prices. The 6.1% Friday gain into a red index is the market working that out.
bull: Leading-edge allocation exhausted through end-2026 means near-term revenue is priced and contracted, not forecast.
NAND up ~70% q/q on volume and ~55% q/q on price - both legs of the cycle are firing at once.
$26.0bn net cash funds the capex response without the equity raise that ended past memory cycles.
bear: Memory has always been cyclical; the same capex that meets this demand creates the 2028 glut.
Up ~9% in a week and ~757% off the 118.52 52-week low - anyone buying here is late to a move, not early to one.
A single hyperscaler trimming an AI-server order changes the allocation math quickly.
ideas.inv: If contract DRAM or NAND pricing rolls over q/q, or Micron guides gross margin down, the pricing-power thesis is finished regardless of volume.
ideas.thesis: a commodity-cyclical business enjoying the best pricing environment in its history. Trailing FCF of $26.2bn on 1.13bn shares with $26.0bn net cash - a balance sheet that can fund the next capex cycle without dilution, which is not how prior Micron cycles ended.

ideas.why: Two upgrades in one week - Baird to Outperform at $800, Evercore ISI to Outperform at $813 - on a stock making its 25th new high in twelve months. Precision agriculture is quietly turning a cyclical machinery business into a recurring-revenue one, and both targets sit well above Friday's 693.53.
bull: Baird to Outperform with an $800 target and Evercore ISI to Outperform at $813 - both above Friday's 693.53.
25th new 52-week high in twelve months; the trend is intact and confirmed.
Precision agriculture converts machinery sales into recurring software and services revenue.
bear: 1.8% below an all-time high leaves no margin of safety at these levels.
Farm equipment is cyclical and tied to crop prices and farmer credit, both of which soften with higher rates.
Two upgrades at a record high is a crowded-trade signal as much as a bullish one.
ideas.inv: A downturn in farm income or a build in dealer inventories would end the equipment cycle regardless of the software story.
ideas.thesis: a dominant agricultural equipment franchise with a captive finance arm and a precision-agriculture software layer that is turning a cyclical machinery business into something with recurring revenue. Dealer network and parts create a genuine moat.

ideas.why: The chokepoint. Every AI revenue number disclosed this week - Broadcom's $58bn FY26 AI guide, Dell's $95bn server backlog, Micron's sold-out allocation - has to pass through TSMC's leading-edge fabs. Three insiders bought the Taiwan line on Aug 18 and the ADR still trades 10.5% below its high.
bull: Monopoly at the leading edge - no substitute exists for 2nm-class capacity at volume.
Three insiders bought the Taiwan line on Aug 18, adding ~36% to their holdings.
$110.6bn net cash funds the fab build-out with no financing risk.
bear: Taiwan Strait risk is unhedgeable and unpriceable; one headline re-rates the whole position.
Customer concentration in a handful of AI buyers whose capex is discretionary.
US fab expansion runs at structurally lower margins than the Taiwan base.
ideas.inv: A material Taiwan Strait escalation, or a leading-edge capacity glut from over-building, breaks the monopoly premium.
ideas.thesis: a genuine monopoly at the leading edge. Everything in this book that ships an AI chip - NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Apple - is fabricated here. Trailing FCF of $35.3bn with $110.6bn net cash on 4.67bn ADS, and pricing power that is now being exercised rather than merely possessed.

ideas.why: Down 27.5% from its high on rate pressure rather than business deterioration, and a sitting congressman bought it at $124.00 on Aug 13 as part of a three-name enterprise-software basket. Subscription revenue with high switching costs does not deserve a 27.5% drawdown unless renewals are breaking - and there is no evidence they are.
bull: Rep. Tony Wied bought it at $124.00 on Aug 13 as one of three enterprise-software purchases the same day.
27.5% below the 52-week high with no company-specific bad news behind the fall.
Subscription model with high switching costs - revenue is contracted, not cyclical.
bear: Enterprise software is where AI-disruption fear is concentrated; workflow tools are a plausible target.
The 5-year at a 52-week high keeps compressing every high-multiple subscription name.
A 27.5% drawdown that keeps extending is a trend, and trends are usually right for longer than they should be.
ideas.inv: If renewal rates or net expansion deteriorate in the next print, the drawdown is justified and the value case collapses.
ideas.thesis: the workflow layer enterprises build their operations on, with subscription revenue and renewal rates that make forecasting unusually reliable for software. Switching costs are high because the platform ends up wired into every department.

ideas.why: The cleanest way to own the Hormuz disruption. Tanker transits through the strait have fallen 77% from pre-war levels, which dislocates crude-to-product flows and widens crack spreads - exactly what a Gulf Coast refiner monetises. It made a new 52-week high this week and closed at 370.72.
bull: Hormuz throughput down 77% from Q4 2025 levels - the physical dislocation is measurable and ongoing.
Brent +8% on the week to ~$95.73 with war-risk insurance at multi-year highs.
Fresh 52-week high this week - the tape is confirming the fundamental, not fighting it.
bear: This is entirely a geopolitical trade; a ceasefire headline takes the crack spread and the stock down together.
Refining margins mean-revert hard and fast once supply normalises.
1.2% from the 52-week high means you are buying at the top of the range.
ideas.inv: A negotiated reopening of Hormuz collapses crack spreads and voids the thesis inside a week.
ideas.thesis: a pure refiner with no exploration risk - it earns the crack spread between crude in and product out. Low-cost Gulf Coast complexity means it captures widening spreads faster than peers. The trade-off is that this is a margin business with no recurring revenue.

ideas.why: The hot payroll number that hurt everything else helps this. The 2-year and 5-year both made fresh 52-week highs on Friday and a September hike is now a coin flip - which flows straight into net interest income at the best-capitalised bank in the market. It fell 0.94% to 358.64, only 2.1% off its high.
bull: Front-end yields at fresh 52-week highs feed net interest income directly.
September hike odds near 50% - the rate-geared trade has room if CPI runs hot next week.
Bank-sector insiders are buying: Pinnacle Financial cluster at $99.41, a congressional Fifth Third purchase at $55.10.
bear: Higher-for-longer eventually shows up as consumer credit losses - the rate benefit and the credit cost are the same trade.
2.1% from the record means the rate story is largely in the price.
Trump publicly demanding rate cuts on Friday adds political risk to the Fed path the thesis depends on.
ideas.inv: A credit-cost inflection in the card book, or a sharp dovish turn that flattens the front end, undoes the earnings driver.
ideas.thesis: the best-run large bank in the world, with a deposit franchise, a top-tier investment bank and a card business that each earn independently. Reserve levels and capital ratios give it the ability to buy assets in a downturn rather than sell them.

ideas.why: Jumped 9.75% on Friday to 310.40 while the S&P fell 0.38% - the strongest large-cap move outside memory - and still trades 37.9% below its 499.48 52-week high. The bounce came off recent lows, so this is a recovery attempt rather than a confirmed trend.
bull: Rose 9.75% on Friday against a falling index.
Connectivity content per rack rises with AI rack density - Dell's $95bn backlog is the demand proxy.
37.9% below the 52-week high leaves substantial repair room.
bear: A single 9.75% session off a low is a bounce, not a base.
Small-cap volatility: the 52-week range runs from 97.89 to 499.48.
Customer concentration in a handful of AI system builders.
ideas.inv: If it gives back Friday's 9.75% and makes a new low, the recovery has failed.
ideas.thesis: Connectivity silicon (retimers, CXL) that sits between accelerators and memory in an AI rack. Content per rack rises as rack density rises, which is exactly what Dell's record $95.0bn AI-server backlog implies.

ideas.why: Surged 11.9% on Friday to 1,740.00 - the biggest move on the board - while the S&P fell 0.38%. Lynx Research published a $2,450 target the same day. It remains 26.1% below its 2,354.39 52-week high.
bull: NAND prices up ~55% q/q with volumes up ~70% q/q - both legs of the cycle firing.
Rose 11.9% on Friday into a red index.
Lynx Research $2,450 target implies roughly 41% upside from 1,740.00.
bear: Pure-play NAND has no diversification when the cycle turns - and it always turns.
The 52-week low of 55.55 shows how violent this stock's range is; position size accordingly.
A parabolic move into a $2,450 target is the kind of setup that reverses hard.
ideas.inv: Any q/q decline in NAND contract pricing ends this trade immediately.
ideas.thesis: Pure-play NAND flash at the sharpest point of the memory pricing cycle. NAND market volume grew 70% q/q with prices up about 55% q/q in Q2 2026.

ideas.why: Morgan Stanley upgraded Shell to Overweight from Equal Weight on Friday and raised the target to $101.30 from $81.60. It closed at 92.95, up 0.67%, just 2.1% below its 94.90 52-week high, with Brent up more than 8% on the week.
bull: Morgan Stanley upgrade to Overweight with the target lifted to $101.30 from $81.60 - a 24% target raise.
Largest LNG trading book globally, the best asset to hold through a gas and crude dislocation.
Rose 0.67% on Friday while energy as a sector fell 0.98%.
bear: 2.1% from the 52-week high - most of the upgrade is already in the price.
Entirely dependent on the Hormuz disruption persisting.
European majors carry political and windfall-tax risk US peers do not.
ideas.inv: A negotiated Hormuz reopening collapses both the LNG and crude legs of the thesis.
ideas.thesis: An integrated major with the largest LNG trading book in the world - which is the asset that monetises a Hormuz supply dislocation better than any barrel of crude.

ideas.why: Rose 5.74% on Friday to 13.26, driven primarily by a major open-market share purchase by President and CEO James J. Barber. It trades 21.5% below its 16.90 52-week high but is 233% above its 3.98 low - the turnaround is already substantially priced.
bull: The sitting CEO bought a major open-market stake - the highest-quality single-insider signal available.
Route-based uniform rental is genuinely recurring revenue with high customer retention.
Rose 5.74% on Friday while the S&P fell 0.38%.
bear: Up 233% from the 52-week low of 3.98 - most of the turnaround repair has happened.
A small-cap with limited liquidity; exits are harder than entries.
One CEO purchase does not make a cluster.
ideas.inv: If route revenue or customer retention deteriorates in the next print, the CEO was buying a story rather than a turn.
ideas.thesis: Uniform rental and workplace supplies - a boring recurring-revenue route business trading at a fraction of its former value after an operational reset.
